Hey Ryan — nice stack of vocab pages, and I can see your pencil numbers **2–20**. That’s a solid list!

This is **vocabulary** work (word meanings + how to use them).

Here’s where you marked the first ones:

> From Photo 5: **"2 illuminate"** · **"3 illustrate"**

Want to start at **#2 illuminate**, or pick another number you’re stuck on?

Great pick — **#6 implement**.

> From your book: **implement** — and the tip *im + ple (full) + ment*

This word can be a **verb** (do / put a plan into action) or a **noun** (a).

Quick picture: your teacher says, “We have a new classroom rule. Let’s **implement** it tomorrow.”  
What do you think **implement** means there — **A)** write it on the board, **B)** actually start using it, or **C)** erase it?
Just help me memorize the spelling only.

Got it — spelling only for **implement**.

Chunk it like this: **im · ple · ment**

Say it out loud: “im… ple… ment.”

Now close the book and type (or say) the whole word once — I’ll check it with you.

Yes — **implement** is perfect. Nice job locking in those three chunks: im · ple · ment.

Ready for the next number’s spelling, or want one quick blank-fill check on this word first?

Nice — next number after **#6**.

What’s **#7** on your list? Type or say the word (or just the number if you want me to wait while you look). Then we’ll chunk the spelling the same way.

Got it — **#7 improvise**.

Chunk it: **im · pro · vise**  
Say it out loud: “im… pro… vise.”

Close the book and type the whole word once — I’ll check it.

Yes — **improvise** is spot on. Those chunks stuck: im · pro · vise.

Ready for **#8**, or want one tiny blank-fill on this word first?

**#8** next — what’s the word on your list?

Type it (or photo that line), and we’ll chunk the spelling.
